title: HC Sean Payton on the challenge of facing Jacksonville’s defense: 'It’s a really talented front 7’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims remains the featured punt returner and kickoff rotation piece, but the Week 2 status question on Mims was left open as Denver faces a talented Jacksonville front seven after a rough opener.
summary: Payton opened by explaining that Denver's short week after a Monday night game is treated like a Wednesday, with recovery prioritized and a somewhat heavier Saturday practice. He took collective blame for the poor opener, saying there was dirt on many hands starting with him, and he deflected questions about Bo Nix by noting many players felt the same way after watching the tape. He praised Jacksonville's defense as well coached and purposeful in creating takeaways, and said patience and ball security at the reception point will be needed against their zone-heavy approach. He called the Jaguars' run front really talented, noting the ends, nose and three-technique, and said the ability to stop the run is a good sign for them. Asked whether he can spark the run game, he said it is both patience and forcing it, comparing it to body shots in boxing. On special teams, he said Marvin Mims will return punts and kickoffs, with the kickoff role varying by game plan. When asked if Mims is in jeopardy for Sunday, he gave a dismissive answer that it's only Wednesday, so no status was given. He also revealed he has a 4-5 disc issue in his back that made standing for the long game painful, but said it's improving. The rest covered Jacksonville's use of Travis Hunter as primarily a defender, Liam Coen's use of his offense, and reminiscences about Brian Dawkins.

title: Matt LaFleur: MarShawn Lloyd has 'shown a lot of confidence that he is able to do it'
headline: MarShawn Lloyd handled his Week 1 workload and hits, and LaFleur says he's building him up, while Van Ness and Hargrave are in concussion protocol and Aaron Banks' availability remains week to week.
summary: LaFleur confirmed Lukas Van Ness entered the concussion protocol Monday and Javon Hargrave on Wednesday, described as residual effects of earlier contact, and said you never know how long concussions will last. Aaron Banks had a good day of work and the team hopes he can practice Thursday, but LaFleur admitted offensive line availability has been an ongoing issue and he can't promise it won't be a season-long thing. On MarShawn Lloyd, he said the Vikings game script limited the run game, but Lloyd did a good job handling the hits and has built up through the offseason, camp and preseason, which gives the coach confidence. He praised the kicker for handling long field goal attempts early but said the offense needs to do a better job so the kicker isn't kicking from so far. He talked about how a steady run game keeps the offense on schedule and avoids obvious passing downs, especially in the tight red zone. He praised Matthew Golden for a downfield block on Christian Watson's long play and said the team wants every player to chase the ball. On Micah Parsons, LaFleur hadn't asked about his status and suggested it could be a couple of weeks. He expects the backups behind Van Ness to be ready if he can't play. He also noted the Jets use many personnel groupings and tight ends, which adds prep.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 17)
headline: Joey is ramping up from a conditioning designation, Troy Fautanu is on a limited plan, and Nick Herbig is being used on and off the ball.
summary: McCarthy was pleased with Joey's work on Wednesday. Joey did everything scheduled and is expected to do more Thursday. The injury report listed him as conditioning, and McCarthy gave no timeline for a full return, saying every player's situation is different. He did not say whether Joey would play Sunday. Troy Fautanu is on a limited plan, and McCarthy only hoped he would get through practice. Max Iheanachor is improving but needs reps after missing padded work. McCarthy praised T.J. Watt's leadership, including the pregame speech, and said he played huge on Sunday. He said Nick Herbig is being used on the edge, on the ball and in space to create targeting problems for offenses, and he expects that to continue. On the Patriots, he praised Drake Maye as more established, composed, comfortable in the pocket and an effective runner. He said linebacker speed gives the defense schematic and personnel flexibility, with the plan set week to week.
